chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad and Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Al-Washa', from Ahmad ibn 'A'idh, from Abu Khadija, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is none from the house wherein is a pigeon, except that the inhabitants of that house would not be hit by an affliction from the Jinn. The foolish ones from the Jinn tend to tamper in the house, so they would be tampering with the pigeons and they would be neglecting the human beings.

key_terms.آفَة: affliction, calamity, or harm; here refers specifically to harmful interference by jinn
key_terms.الْجِنّ: the jinn; a class of beings mentioned in the Quran, created from smokeless fire, sharing the world with humans
key_terms.حَمَام: pigeon (domesticated dove); keeping them was a traditional practice, and this hadith attributes a spiritual protective benefit to their presence in the home
key_terms.سُفَهَاء: the foolish or witless ones; implies not all jinn are harmful, only the undiscerning among them

ai.seo_question: Does keeping pigeons in the home protect against jinn according to Imam al-Sadiq in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that keeping pigeons in one's home provides protection from the harmful mischief of foolish jinn. The Imam explains the mechanism: reckless jinn who enter homes are drawn to pigeons and occupy themselves with them, thereby leaving the human residents unharmed. This hadith reflects the early Islamic cosmological understanding that jinn inhabit the same physical spaces as humans and that certain birds may serve as spiritual buffers.
